findings.title: First save destroys opaque metadata on imported condition expressions
findings.why_it_matters: The retained serializer promises to preserve imported moddle content outside the typed mutation surface, but every typed conditional sequence flow has its conditionExpression replaced with a newly created object. Merely importing, saving, reopening, or renaming an unrelated element therefore deletes valid expression identity and extension semantics that the API never exposed or asked to change.
findings.suggested_fix: For an existing retained sequence flow, mutate only the typed condition fields on its existing conditionExpression and preserve its id, documentation, extensionElements, custom attributes, and other moddle-owned state. Create a new FormalExpression only for a newly created condition, and introduce explicit managed/dirty state before supporting condition replacement or clearing.
evidence: readConnection reduces an imported expression to body/type/language/evaluatesToTypeRef at src/core/BpmnDocument.ts:1445-1460, so expression id, documentation, extensionElements, and custom attributes have no typed representation.

serializeRetained calls applyConnectionProperties for every indexed connection, and src/core/BpmnDocument.ts:855 unconditionally assigns semantic.conditionExpression = moddle.create(...), even when the condition was imported and no condition mutation occurred.

Concrete reproduction: import a task-to-task sequence flow whose bpmn:FormalExpression has id=Expr_1, documentation 'keep me', and a vendor:metadata extension, then immediately export. Before import, bpmn-moddle resolves Expr_1 and both child structures; after the engine's import autosave/export, Expr_1, documentation, and extensionElements are all absent while only the body remains.

Because importXml immediately runs commitMutation and persists the reconciled XML, the loss occurs before the caller can inspect or reopen the imported document; subsequent save/reopen cycles cannot recover it from sourceXml.

findings.title: Alias precedence persists a different default-flow decision than the request expresses
findings.why_it_matters: The engine correctly rejects conflicting isDefault/default values, but the MCP handler collapses three spellings before the engine sees them, while updateElement independently applies nullish precedence to two flow-ID spellings. Contradictory or invalid aliases are therefore silently ignored, so a request to create a default can create an ordinary flow and an explicit request to clear a default can instead assign another flow; autosave makes that unintended routing durable.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalize aliases with one shared presence-based resolver before mutation: validate every supplied alias, reject disagreement, and preserve explicit null as the clear operation. Pass both supported connect aliases to the engine conflict check or remove undocumented handler aliases; apply the same conflict rule to defaultFlow/default during update.
evidence: At src/server/handlers.ts:375, isDefault ?? args.default ?? args.defaultFlow discards all lower-priority supplied values. Thus {isDefault:false, default:true} reaches the engine only as isDefault:false, bypassing SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:196-198, which would reject the conflict if both values were preserved.

Concrete handler reproduction: connect a task to a target with {isDefault:false, default:true}. The call succeeds, creates one sequence flow, and leaves source.defaultFlow undefined; the saved XML and reopened model therefore encode an ordinary flow despite one alias explicitly requesting a default. An invalid lower-priority alias is masked in the same way.

At src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:390-423, updateElement detects either properties.defaultFlow or properties.default but resolves them with defaultFlow ?? default and never compares aliases. {defaultFlow:F1, default:F2} silently assigns F1, and {defaultFlow:null, default:F2} silently assigns F2 rather than clearing.
All of these paths run inside commitMutation, so successful alias mis-resolution is serialized and atomically saved instead of remaining a transient response-format inconsistency.

residual_risks: Imported defaults or conditions on valid constructs outside the typed index remain intentionally invisible to list/get responses; later typed ownership transitions must continue distinguishing opaque retained references from explicitly cleared managed references.

ProcessContext exposes mutable element and connection maps, so an in-process caller can bypass source ownership, supported-source, and default-versus-condition checks and rely only on late serializer rejection.

Imported BpmnConditionExpression.type remains an unrestricted moddle type string; direct typed-model mutation can request an abstract or unknown type even though MCP condition creation restricts the value.
testing_gaps: No round-trip fixture gives a conditionExpression its own id, documentation, extensionElements, vendor attributes, or other opaque children and compares them after import autosave, unrelated update, save, and reopen.

No table-driven tests cover every connect alias permutation, conflicting booleans, masked invalid lower-priority values, or update defaultFlow/default conflicts including explicit null clearing, with memory, XML, and reopen assertions.
Default lifecycle coverage does not delete the active default flow's target after import/reopen and verify source cleanup in get_element, persisted XML, and a second reopen.

Unsupported conditional-flow coverage exercises a start event and an inferred message flow, but not explicit associations/message flows or independently authored invalid message/association condition XML.
No retained import fixture exercises a FormalExpression evaluatesToTypeRef together with an opaque ItemDefinition and verifies the reference plus expression metadata across mutation and reopen.
